title.narrative: Integrated Nutrition and Health Assistance for Vulnerable Populations in MMC, Jere, Bama and Monguno LGA in Borno State Lean Season Response”

description.narrative: ltpgtThe IRC proposed integrated impact-driven Nutrition and Health intervention seeks to address the increased acute malnutrition and deteriorating health conditions of Internally Displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities in Bama, Mongonu, MMC, and Jere, LGAs of Borno State, Nigeria during the lean season period. Nutrition interventions will focus on SAM and MAM prevention and treatment by supporting three(3) Stabilization Centers (SC), 16 Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP), community-based Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFP). With funding from the NHF, the IRC will v provide quality care to SAM children with complications at three functional Stabilization Centers in MMC, Jere and Bama. To meet the expected Lean season, increase in cases of malnutrition, IRC will maintain expansion of bed capacity at Bama Stabilization Center (SC) to its maximum of 70 bed capacity and increase capacity at Umaru Shehu SC from 30 to 70 beds. The project will also maintain operations at Mashamari SC, which has a 60-bed capacity, and continue running 16 Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) – 3 in Bama, 5 in MMC/Jere, and 8 in Monguno. IRC staff will collaborate with Ministry of Health personnel, community health volunteers (CHVs), Family MUAC groups, and Mother-to-Mother Support Groups (MtMSGs) to screen and refer children for acute malnutrition. A key complementary initiative integrated into this intervention is the empowering of caregivers and mothers whose malnourished children are receiving treatment at the Stabilization centers with short-term financial literacy training and income generation activities, aimed at reducing malnutrition relapses and improving household food security. For the Health component, the intervention will support a total of 12 PHCs across MMC and Jere ( 5) Mongonu (4) and Bama (3), providing essential primary and reproductive health services, including Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI), communicable and non-communicable disease treatment, antenatal/postnatal care (ANC/PNC), immunization, treatment for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), family planning, obstetric/neonatal care, and support for sexual assault survivors. Health system support includes training health workers, supplying essential medicines, ensuring ambulance referral services, and reinforcing supervisory oversight. The IRC will also strengthen community-based surveillance through the use of trained community health workers who will carry out morbidity and mortality surveillance tracking and reporting notifiable diseases. In addition, through ongoing continuous monitoring and analysis of disease trends, endemic diseases such as malaria, acute watery diarrhea arrhea/cholera and measles will be monitored. In situations of increased morbidities or even declared outbreaks the IRC will adapt its services to be responsive to the outbreak needs. As the rainy season approaches the risk of a cholera outbreak is anticipated. To respond to the possible cholera outbreak, the IRC plans to set up Oral rehydration points ORPs for case management and carry out risk communication and community engagement activities through the development and dissemination of information, education and communication materials, and provision of community health education on prevention of cholera.ltbrgtlt/pgt
